headline: Washington proposes tariffs on 14 economies, Gulf oil sites come under drone fire, and Asian chip stocks plunge as AI doubts return.

items.title: US proposes new tariffs on 14 economies
items.summary: The US Trade Representative proposed Section 301 tariffs on goods from 14 economies over industrial overcapacity, with Vietnam facing up to 35%, India up to 25%, China up to 20% and the EU 15%. These are proposals only; public comments are due by 5 January 2027.
items.why: Tariff shifts change trade routes and prices for exporters and importers, including in West Africa.

items.title: Houthi drones target Saudi oil refinery as Gulf tensions rise
items.summary: Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed four drones over the Ras Tanura refinery area, a day after a Houthi drone hit Riyadh's tallest tower and injured at least 11 people. The Houthis threatened Red Sea ports after a coalition strike on Hodeidah; separately, Iran said tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
items.why: Attacks on Gulf oil routes push up fuel prices, which feed into Ghana's transport and food costs.
items.videoQuery: Houthi drones Ras Tanura Riyadh tower

items.title: Israeli strike kills Hamas security chief and family in Gaza
items.summary: An Israeli strike killed Hamas interior security chief Mohammad Abuelouf along with his wife and two children, according to the Hamas-run health ministry and medics. In Israel, opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot secured his first coalition partner ahead of elections.
items.source: Reuters via Just Security; Al Jazeera
items.videoQuery: Gaza strike Hamas security chief November 2026

items.title: Bangladesh garment workers win a 36% minimum-wage rise
items.summary: After weeks of protests, Bangladesh's wage board agreed to raise the garment sector's monthly minimum from 12,500 to 17,500 taka (about $136), taking effect in December. Workers had demanded 30,000 taka, so it is unclear whether protests will end.
items.videoQuery: Bangladesh garment workers minimum wage protests 2026

items.title: Who is to blame for COP31's 'failure'?
items.summary: A Carbon Brief media round-up says COP31 in Antalya overran by two days and the presidency's 'Antalya pact' cover decision was rejected by at least 32 countries, including the EU and UK. Many other decisions were adopted; most coverage blamed oil-producing states, while Chinese state media presented China as constructive.
items.why: Article 6 work continues regardless of the cover decision, so carbon market rules still matter for Ghana.

items.title: Earth logs its most abnormally hot day on record
items.summary: Preliminary Copernicus data show the global average temperature on 20 November was 2.12°C above pre-industrial levels, beating the previous daily record of 2.07°C from November 2023. The WMO expects the current El Niño to peak in December.
items.why: El Niño years often bring heat and rainfall shifts to West Africa that affect fish catches and smoking.
items.videoQuery: Copernicus record hot day El Nino November 2026

items.title: 2026 likely to tie 2024 as the warmest year
items.summary: Carbon Brief's analysis of six datasets puts 2026 at about 1.52°C above pre-industrial, with a 67% chance of beating 2024. It projects 2027 at about 1.74°C, with a 96% chance of setting a new record.

items.title: Carbon Market Watch: Article 6 rules intact, but the 2028 review is the next fight
items.summary: The NGO says the Article 6 rulebook survived COP31 unchanged, but warns that industry lobbying grew compared with COP30 and will target the major Article 6 review planned for 2028.
items.why: Directly relevant to your Article 6 research: integrity rules shape which Ghanaian credits buyers will trust.

items.title: Mahama hands three new aircraft to the Ghana Air Force
items.summary: President Mahama is due to hand over two Airbus helicopters (ACH175 and ACH160) and a Dassault Falcon 6X long-range jet at the Air Force Base in Accra on 26 November. The purchases were approved by Parliament in December 2025, according to the Ghana Armed Forces.
items.videoQuery: Ghana Air Force new aircraft Mahama

items.title: Ghana to recruit 10,000 health workers
items.summary: Health Minister Mintah Akandoh said the government will begin recruiting 10,000 health workers next week. Separately, the Cyber Security Authority warned Black Friday shoppers after online fraud losses reached GH¢1.7m.

items.title: Tinubu pledges peace in Nigeria's northeast ahead of January vote
items.summary: At a rally in Maiduguri, President Tinubu promised to restore peace to the insurgency-hit northeast as he seeks re-election on 16 January. He said more than 70 schoolchildren abducted in Borno this year are still held; analysts say security gains are not yet proven.

items.title: DR Congo rebels halt advance on Bunia
items.summary: The CRP rebel group led by Thomas Lubanga said it would stop its push toward Bunia in Ituri and withdraw from recently seized areas after heavy clashes with the army. The WHO said fighting near a hospital forced health workers out, disrupting the Ebola response.
items.videoQuery: DR Congo CRP rebels Bunia Ituri

items.title: Asian chip stocks plunge as AI doubts return
items.summary: South Korea's Kospi fell 6.2% and Taiwan's Taiex 4.8% as a rally sparked by Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO reversed; Samsung and SK Hynix dropped around 10–11%. On Wall Street the Nasdaq recovered from a 4% morning drop to close slightly lower, with Nvidia down about 3.9%.
items.videoQuery: Asian markets plunge Nvidia AI stocks November 2026

items.title: US growth revised up, but inflation heats up
items.summary: The US economy grew at a 4.3% annual rate in the third quarter, revised up from 3.4%, while October PCE prices rose 3.8% from a year earlier (3.3% excluding food and energy). Markets increasingly expect a Federal Reserve rate rise in December.
items.why: Higher US rates tend to strengthen the dollar and put pressure on the cedi.
items.videoQuery: US PCE inflation October 2026 GDP revision

items.title: Nvidia's credit rating put on watch
items.summary: S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia's AA credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade, days after its board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO.

items.title: Pakistan's first astronaut reaches China's space station
items.summary: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali became the first Pakistani in orbit and the first foreign astronaut to board China's Tiangong station, after launching on Shenzhou-24 from Jiuquan. He is expected to stay 5 to 10 days.
items.why: Shows how China is opening its space programme to partner countries in the Global South.

items.title: Euclid telescope finds its first new comet
items.summary: ESA's Euclid space telescope, built to map dark matter and dark energy, has spotted its first previously unknown comet.

items.title: A hard-to-treat depression subtype identified
items.summary: Researchers describe a subtype of severe depression, affecting about one in four people with the condition, that responds poorly to common antidepressants.

good.title: Borno school enrolment nearly doubles
good.summary: School enrolment in Nigeria's Borno State rose to about 1.42 million in 2025 from about 767,000 in 2017-18, state figures show, with 104 new schools built. Out-of-school children fell to roughly 800,000 from an estimated 2.2 million at the crisis peak.

good.title: 100 MW solar plant to power Tema Free Zone factories
good.summary: LMI Holdings secured $88.6 million, backed by IFC, IDA, EAAIF and Ninety One, for a 100 MWp solar plant at Dawa, Ghana. It is expected to produce about 129.5 GWh a year for more than 95 manufacturers in the Tema Free Zone.
good.why: Proof that solar for productive use is bankable in Ghana: a useful example for your pitches.

good.title: Zimbabwe's business solar pipeline tops 1.5 GW
good.summary: Zimbabwe now has 251.4 MW of commercial and industrial solar running, with about 1.5 GW more under construction, in financing or in development, according to AFSIA data.

good.title: Bangladesh garment workers get a pay rise
good.summary: Four million garment workers will see their monthly minimum wage rise 36% from December after weeks of protests.

good.title: World energy efficiency improves faster
good.summary: The IEA's Energy Efficiency 2026 report expects global energy intensity to improve by nearly 3% this year, up from about 2% in 2025.

future.title: Clean cooking financed by carbon credits
future.why: New government policies across Africa have helped secure about $900 million in new clean-cooking finance, with carbon credits as the main engine. The catch: it only lasts if buyers trust the credits.
future.fit: This is Carbon Clarity's core. The winners will be projects with measured, audit-ready data.
future.step: This month: map which Gold Standard metered-method requirements your pilot data already meets.

future.title: Digital MRV and high-integrity credit data
future.why: Credit buyers increasingly pay only for credits they can verify. Sensor-based monitoring and clean data trails are becoming the difference between credits that sell and credits that don't.
future.fit: Your Data Vault idea could become a service for other cookstove and agriculture projects in Ghana.
future.step: Write a one-page description of the Data Vault as a service: who pays, what it proves.

future.title: Clean heat for small industries
future.why: RMI lists clean industrial heat among Africa's six emerging climate-tech opportunities. Fish smoking is exactly this: small-scale process heat.
future.fit: Improved ovens for fish processors are a clean-heat business with income for women, not just a stove programme.
future.step: Estimate the market: how many processors in Greater Accra and coastal Ghana, and how much wood they burn.

future.title: Carbon removal from biomass: biochar
future.why: RMI also highlights carbon dioxide removal that uses Africa's biomass and soils, a market where removal credits sell for far more than avoidance credits.
future.fit: Waste biomass from smoking (husks, offcuts) could be turned into biochar: a second revenue stream.
future.step: Read one biochar removal methodology and list what you'd need to measure.

future.title: Energy-led climate tech is where African investment goes
future.why: Africa's climate-tech startups raised $6.35bn from 2016 to 2025, now the continent's biggest venture sector, with energy taking about 65% of the money.
future.fit: Pitch Carbon Clarity as energy plus livelihoods: efficient heat, solar drying or cold storage for fish.
future.step: Add one slide to your pitch: 'Why energy investors should care about fish smoking'.

future.title: Article 6 advisory for Ghanaian projects
future.why: Ghana is one of the first countries trading credits between governments under Article 6. Developers need people who understand authorisation, corresponding adjustments and the Carbon Market Office process.
future.fit: Your Ghana carbon market research makes you one of those people: it can become consulting work or a job.
future.step: Turn your Step 3 agreement table into a two-page brief you can share on LinkedIn.
